pbContract: _superusers는 시스템 auth collection이다. 공통 record CRUD/인증과 collection auth 설정을 쓰며 JWT와 전역 SuperuserIPs 정책을 사용한다.
pgImplementation: 별도 admins/admin_sessions 모델, 일회 setup token, Argon2id 비밀번호, 서버 저장 opaque cookie/bearer session, CSRF와 관리자별 CIDR 허용목록을 제공한다.
gap: 관리자 기능은 존재하지만 _superusers record CRUD/collection OAuth·OTP·MFA 설정 모델이나 정적 superuser JWT를 대체하지 않는다. 별도 관리자 모델은 의도적 구조 차이이며 PB API 1:1은 아니다.

pbContract: _superusers도 일반 auth MFA 흐름을 사용한다. 첫 password/OAuth2/OTP 인증 후 mfaId를 발급하고 다른 인증 방식으로 동일 사용자임을 확인한다.
pgImplementation: 관리자 password login은 등록된 TOTP를 함께 검증한다. 관리자 email OTP는 CLI 발급 코드의 별도 로그인 경로다.
gap: PB의 mfaId와 두 로그인 방식 조합, 조건부 _superusers MFA 설정이 없다. CLI-issued OTP 로그인은 TOTP를 호출하지 않는 별도 관리 경로로, 무권한 원격 우회가 확인된 것은 아니다.

pbContract: 서로 독립적인 auth collection에 record와 collection별 인증 정책을 둔다.
pgImplementation: auth_collections별 사용자 identity/session/policy를 분리한다. metadata users+profile 저장과 collection 공개 record ID 정책으로 구현한다.
gap: PostgreSQL 공유 metadata 모델과 UUID 내부 identity가 PB collection table 모델을 대체한다. 이름별 격리는 테스트가 있으나 이름/ID 라우팅 차이는 AUTH-13에 별도 기록한다.

pbContract: Auth record는 일반 collection field 타입·제약·인덱스·relation/file을 가진다. OAuth createData와 일반 CRUD도 동일 record validation을 따른다.
pgImplementation: 최대64 custom typed fields를 JSON profile에 저장하며 scalar/JSON/geo/relation/file/password 등을 검증하고 CRUD·규칙을 적용한다.
gap: custom field ID, Unique, Default를 거부하며 auth field 타입·옵션 모델이 PB와 같지 않다. 공통 record index/field 변경 모델이 아니며 public 가입 payload에 custom fields를 전달할 수 없다.

pbContract: 일반 POST collection records가 auth 가입이다. createRule와 전체 record field validation, password/passwordConfirm 및 custom data를 적용하고 생성 record를 반환한다.
pgImplementation: 별도 /register가 email/password만 받아 registrationEnabled와 createRule를 검사하고 사용자 및 session을 생성한다.
gap: custom fields/명시적 공개 id/passwordConfirm/emailVisibility 등 PB 가입 record payload를 지원하지 않는다. 가입과 로그인 session 발급이 결합되고 OAuth 가입의 createRule 경로는 AUTH-34에 별도 기록한다.

pbContract: 설정된 identityFields에서 검색하며 요청 identityField로 특정 필드를 선택할 수 있다. single-column unique index의 NOCASE collation을 존중한다.
pgImplementation: email 및 선언된 visible text profile field를 순서대로 검색하고 identity uniqueness를 service에서 검증한다.
gap: 요청별 identityField 선택이 없고 text profile 비교는 고정 exact comparison이다. PB unique-index/collation 계약과 hidden field 허용 범위를 그대로 제공하지 않는다.

pbContract: PasswordField.Min은 문자(rune) 수 기준이고 설정 범위는 1..71이다.
pgImplementation: collection minimumPasswordBytes를 12..128 bytes로 제한하고 자격 증명 작성·로그인에 적용한다.
gap: 짧은 비밀번호를 허용하는 PB 정책을 표현할 수 없으며 다중바이트 문자열의 길이 의미가 다르다. 강한 기본 정책과 호환 범위 차이를 구별해야 한다.

pbContract: identity/password 검증 후 authRule·MFA를 적용하고 JWT와 record를 반환한다. 알려지지 않은 identity에도 비밀번호 검증을 수행한다.
pgImplementation: 계정·네트워크 제한, dummy Argon2id 검증, 잠긴 최신 사용자 상태 재확인 후 authRule·MFA와 opaque session 발급을 적용한다.
gap: 기본 비밀번호 로그인 기능은 구현되어 있지만 wire 응답(user/expiresAt), Argon2id, DB session 방식은 의도적으로 다르다. identity 선택·정책·MFA 범위는 AUTH-06/07/18/30에 따로 기록한다.

pbContract: refreshable JWT는 새 JWT를 발급하되 이전 JWT를 개별 폐기하지 않는다. static token은 그대로 반환하고 authRule를 재검사한다.
pgImplementation: 일반 session row의 token hash를 원자적으로 교체하며 이전 bearer는 즉시 무효화된다. 같은 session ID를 유지하며 sliding TTL을 연장하고 authRule를 재검사한다.
gap: refresh 기능은 stateful rotation으로 의도적으로 변경되었다. 이전 token 재시도와 병렬 refresh가 PB처럼 동작하지 않으며 impersonation refresh는 거절한다(AUTH-26).

pbContract: auth endpoint 목록에 session logout/revoke가 없다. JWT는 record tokenKey/collection secret/expiry에 묶이며 key 변경으로 기존 token들을 무효화한다.
pgImplementation: logout은 해당 session을 revoke하고 관리자/사용자 lifecycle은 session 목록 전체 폐기와 credential 변경 시 폐기를 지원한다.
gap: 명시적 서버 session revoke는 PB의 stateless 토큰 모델보다 추가된 기능이다. PB tokenKey와 session 단위 폐기는 같은 단위가 아니다.

pbContract: password enabled/identityFields, OTP·MFA enabled/duration, OAuth displayName/logo/state/authURL/PKCE 값과 legacy 필드를 공개한다.
pgImplementation: public methods에 password/OTP/MFA enabled, identityFields 및 provider name/startEndpoint를 제공하고 민감 설정을 숨긴다.
gap: OTP/MFA duration과 provider 표시명/logo가 없다. authURL·state·PKCE는 별도 시작 endpoint 구조로 바뀌며 PB auth-methods 응답을 그대로 제공하지 않는다.

pbContract: collection OAuth2.Providers는 공식 provider factories와 custom endpoints/scopes/PKCE/extra 설정, mappedFields를 가진다.
pgImplementation: realm별 encrypted client secret, endpoints/scopes/redirect allowlist/claim names/issuer/JWKS 설정을 저장한다. HTTP exchange와 여러 provider profile normalizer가 있다.
gap: PB provider factory 설정 전체를 구현한 것이 아니다. PKCE를 항상 보내고 PB provider별 extra/PKCE toggle/mappedFields와 일부 token/userInfo 교환 특성은 없다. 명칭이 존재하는 normalizer만으로 실제 provider login parity를 입증할 수 없다.

pbContract: collection 경로는 auth collection 이름 또는 ID를 받으며 refresh는 같은 collection의 auth만 허용한다.
pgImplementation: 공개 /api/v1/auth/{authCollection} 경로는 validated collection name으로 찾고 session의 collection을 확인한다. OAuth state에도 realm을 저장한다.
gap: 이름 경로의 격리는 구현됐지만 PB name-or-ID 라우팅과 동일하지 않다. UUID collection ID를 public realm 경로로 사용할 수 없다.

pbContract: 기존 provider 관계, 로그인한 동일 collection 사용자, provider email의 기존 사용자 순서로 연결한다. createData로 신규 record를 만들고 검증 상태에 따라 password/external links 보호 처리를 한다.
pgImplementation: provider+subject+realm에 묶은 stateful PKCE 흐름, 신규 OAuth 사용자 생성, 현재 비밀번호에 묶인 명시적 link를 구현한다. 같은 email의 기존 사용자는 충돌로 처리한다.
gap: 이메일 기반 자동 연결, 로그인 session만으로 OAuth-only 사용자 추가 link, createData 및 기존 사용자 empty-email/verified 동기화가 PB와 다르다. 명시적 연결 정책 자체는 의도적인 보안 선택이나 PB 전체 사용 흐름은 누락된다.

pbContract: _externalAuths record list/view/delete 규칙에 따라 자신의 연결을 조회·삭제할 수 있으며 일반 system-record CRUD를 사용한다.
pgImplementation: 현재 사용자 provider 목록과 unlink, 관리자 auxiliary 삭제를 제공하며 계정 row lock과 마지막 로그인 수단 보존 검사를 적용한다.
gap: 마지막 OAuth 로그인 수단 삭제를 거부하는 추가 정책이 있고 PB _externalAuths 범용 CRUD/filter 응답 계약은 없다. PB의 연결 record providerId/collectionRef/recordRef 정보도 축약된다.

pbContract: OAuth mappedFields로 provider id/name/username/avatarURL을 custom field에 넣고 createData가 우선한다. avatar 대상이 file이면 내려받아 일반 record file로 저장한다.
pgImplementation: provider별 subject/verified email/avatar URL 정규화와 신규 가입 시 제한된 avatar download/storage를 제공한다.
gap: name/username/id를 임의 collection field로 매핑하거나 createData로 덮어쓰는 기능이 없다. avatar는 별도 blob 저장(2MiB,4096px)이며 일반 auth file field로 매핑되지 않는다.

pbContract: 가변 길이 OTP(default8), 10..86400초 TTL, 실패 횟수 제한, 단회 소모를 제공한다. 성공 시 보낸 주소와 현재 email이 같으면 verified로 전환하며 MFA 비활성 시 password를 무작위화한다.
pgImplementation: 고정6자리 HMAC OTP, 신규 발급 시 이전 코드 consume, realm 정책 TTL/최대시도, 잠금·단회 소모 및 등록된 TOTP challenge를 제공한다.
gap: 코드 길이·TTL·재발급 의미가 다르며 OTP 성공 경로에는 PB의 verified 갱신/조건부 password 무작위화가 보이지 않는다. 코드가 특정 email snapshot에 묶여 있지 않은 점도 별도 회귀 검증이 필요하다.

pbContract: password/OAuth2/OTP 중 서로 다른 두 authMethod를 동일 collection/record에서 성공하면 mfaId를 소비하고 token을 발급한다. TOTP enrollment가 전제되지 않는다.
pgImplementation: 비밀번호/OAuth/OTP 첫 단계 후 활성 TOTP factor가 있을 때 challenge를 발급하고 TOTP 또는 recovery code로 완료한다. challenge/코드 재사용을 막는다.
gap: TOTP/recovery 방식은 구현되어 있으나 PB password+email OTP, OAuth+password 등 조합은 없다. MFAEnabled여도 활성 factor가 없는 사용자에게 challenge가 생기지 않는 코드 계약이며 이를 미등록 사용자에 대한 PB식 강제 MFA와 혼동하면 안 된다.

pbContract: MFA.Rule은 full record filter이며 requestInfo·record·relation을 평가한다. 비어 있으면 전체 사용자에게 MFA를 요구한다.
pgImplementation: 빈 규칙 또는 {field,equals} JSON scalar equality만 허용하고 verified/custom profile field를 비교한다. 활성 factor가 있을 때만 평가한다.
gap: PB filter 문법, 복합식/관계/request 조건을 지원하지 않는다. 빈 규칙의 의미도 등록 factor 조건에 의해 더 좁다. 현재 테스트는 full PB 조건 정책을 검증하지 않는다.

pbContract: Public POST /api/collections/{collection}/request-password-reset accepts a validated email only when collection PasswordAuth.Enabled is true. Unknown accounts and recently sent requests receive 204; successful sends establish an in-memory two-minute resend suppression. Delivery runs in the background.
pgImplementation: Public default/named-realm request-password-reset endpoints normalize email, apply account/network buckets, issue a hashed opaque action token, attempt mail synchronously, and suppress unknown-account/delivery failure disclosure.
gap: Collection path and error/throttling behavior differ. The reviewed PgBase request path has no collection PasswordEnabled check; unlike PB it can issue a reset while password authentication is disabled. Invalid email is nondisclosing success rather than PB validation error. PB's two-minute resend suppression and asynchronous delivery are absent from this path.

pbContract: Public collection-scoped confirmation requires token, password and matching passwordConfirm; validates token purpose and collection, saves the new password, and marks an unverified record verified only if its current email still matches the token email claim. Saving password rotates the record token key.
pgImplementation: Confirmation accepts token/newPassword, validates the realm password policy, consumes a purpose-bound, expiring, password-hash-bound database token once, updates password_hash and revokes sessions.
gap: PgBase does not set verified=true after a successful reset, so PB workflows that use password reset as email proof remain unverified. It has no passwordConfirm field or collection-scoped confirm URL, and opaque database tokens are not PB JWTs.

pbContract: Public collection-scoped request accepts email, validates it, conceals missing accounts with 204, suppresses repeat sends for two minutes and skips already-verified records; public confirmation requires a collection-bound verification token, checks its email claim, and returns 204. Superuser verification routes reject because superusers are already verified.
pgImplementation: Request requires an authenticated non-impersonated user session; public confirmation consumes an opaque single-use token and sets that user verified. Already verified users do not receive another verification mail. Native action page supports explicit submit.
gap: No public email-address verification-request contract or collection-scoped confirmation path. Reusing a consumed token fails, while PB accepts a still-valid verification token for an already-verified record. Additional verification trust-transition and email-binding checks are isolated in AUTH-35/36 below; their PgBase consequences are static observations, not executed reproductions.

pbContract: Authenticated record requests a unique different newEmail without a password; public confirmation requires token plus current password, verifies token collection and newEmail, then saves the new email and verified=true. Email changes rotate the record token key.
pgImplementation: Authenticated non-impersonated user supplies currentPassword and newEmail at request time; the new email receives a purpose-bound, password-hash-bound token. Public token-only confirmation updates email/verified and revokes sessions.
gap: Password proof is moved from confirmation to request, so PB request/confirmation payloads and user flow cannot be used unchanged. PgBase checks collisions with other users but does not reject requesting the user's same current email as PB does. Confirm endpoints and token formats differ.

pbContract: PB record CRUD restricts direct verified/email changes to superusers or callers allowed by a nonempty manageRule, in addition to normal record access. A matching manageRule is evaluated against any authenticated record; PB's built-in auth fields do not include a separate active boolean.
pgImplementation: PgBase provides administrator verified/active/session-revoke operations and typed auth-record CRUD. Sensitive user-driven updates require both update rule and a nonempty manage rule evaluated with distinct actor/target; tests reject a manager from another realm. Native active=false revokes sessions.
gap: The old report's claim that delegated manageRule was absent is obsolete. Current PgBase has it, but same-realm actor policy is narrower than PB's authenticated-record rule context; native active/session administration is an adaptation rather than a PB built-in active-field equivalent.

pbContract: When collection AuthAlert.Enabled and a real auth method is present, PB fingerprints real IP plus truncated User-Agent, skips alert on first origin, alerts subsequent new origins, records or updates origin only after the helper succeeds, and keeps up to five origins. Alert delivery failure is logged without failing authentication.
pgImplementation: Successful auth flows record an HMAC fingerprint of network address, atomically deduplicate concurrent origins, update last-seen, and send best-effort mail when an auth_alert template exists. User auxiliary list/get/delete routes and administrator extension queries exist.
gap: Same-IP devices with different User-Agents are not distinguished. Template presence replaces PB's enabled flag/default template. The reviewed insertion path has no first-origin suppression or five-origin pruning, records an origin even when mail fails, and exposes a different auxiliary record/route schema. The old statement that users cannot list origins is obsolete.

pbContract: superuser가 대상 auth record의 nonrefreshable static JWT를 발급한다. duration>=0이며0은 collection 기본값, 별도 짧은 최대값이 없고 관리자 session에 종속되지 않는다.
pgImplementation: 1..15분 impersonation session을 발급하며 actor admin session과 target에 묶고 admin expiry/정책 TTL로 상한을 제한한다.
gap: 장기간 static token/0 duration 기본값/관리자 session 독립 사용과 refresh 반환 계약을 제공하지 않는다. actor-bound 짧은 세션은 의도적 정책이지만 PB impersonation 전체 범위와 같지 않다.

pbContract: meta/oauth2-providers는 등록된 모든 provider를 order/name으로 정렬하여 name, displayName, logo를 반환한다.
pgImplementation: helper는 google/github/microsoft 세 starter configuration의 endpoint와 scope를 items envelope로 반환한다.
gap: 공식 전체 provider inventory가 아니며 displayName/logo/order가 없다. 30여 profile normalizer가 있다는 사실과 helper inventory 범위를 구별해야 한다.

pbContract: 입력 clientId/teamId/keyId/PKCS8 privateKey/duration(1..15777000)으로 Apple audience ES256 JWT를 만들어 secret 필드로 반환한다.
pgImplementation: 동일 claim·ES256·최대 lifetime의 secret 생성 helper가 있다. Team/Key ID는10자리 영숫자, P256 PKCS8만 허용하며 비밀키를 저장하지 않는다.
gap: 핵심 secret 생성 기능은 구현됐다. endpoint/envelope와 stricter key/id validation은 의도적 차이다. 서명 검증 테스트가 있으나 Apple 외부 인증 서버에 실제 교환한 검증은 아니다.

feature: PB auth auxiliary system record handling
pbContract: _externalAuths/_mfas/_otps/_authOrigins는 system collection record/proxy이며 공통 CRUD/filter/pagination과 record hooks를 사용한다. MFA record는 진행 중인 첫 인증 challenge다.
pgImplementation: 관리자·manage-rule 사용자용 auxiliary list/get/delete와 bounded helper query를 제공한다. secrets를 숨기고 PostgreSQL metadata row를 요약한다.
gap: mfas는 PB 진행 challenge 대신 TOTP enrollment factor를 가리킨다. 범용 system record CRUD/filter/pagination/필드·hook 모델과 동일하지 않으며 select summary로 제한된다.

feature: 사용자 암호의 최대 길이·pattern·hash cost 옵션
pbContract: PasswordField Max(default71), Pattern, bcrypt Cost를 field 설정으로 제공하고 길이는 rune 단위다. bcrypt 입력 바이트는 잘라 사용한다.
pgImplementation: realm maximumPasswordBytes/pattern을 지원하며 기본 credential hash는 고정 Argon2id다. service 정책 상한4096이지만 public validatePassword는1024 bytes를 허용한다.
gap: credential hash cost를 realm별 설정할 수 없고 byte/rune 및 최대값 의미가 다르다. 설정 가능한4096과 public 경로 실제1024 상한도 일치하지 않는다. custom password field의 bcrypt 설정은 계정 로그인 credential cost와 별개다.

pbContract: auth/reset/emailChange/verification/file 목적별 secret과10..94670856초 duration을 collection에 저장하고 record tokenKey와 결합해 JWT를 만든다.
pgImplementation: session/verify/password_reset/email_change/otp/impersonation 목적별 암호화 key/version과60..86400초 TTL을 제공한다. rotation과 duration-only update를 구분한다.
gap: realm별 file-token secret/TTL 목적이 없고 TTL 범위가 PB의 기본5일 auth token도 표현하지 못한다. record tokenKey·JWT와 versioned stateful token 의미가 다르다.

pbContract: emailVisibility=false일 때 일반 공개 record에서 email을 숨기되 owner/superuser/실행된 manageRule에 해당하는 actor는 볼 수 있다.
pgImplementation: record의 visibility flag와 owner/admin/active same-realm manager 공개 예외를 구현하고 응답 email을 제거한다.
gap: same-realm manager로 제한되어 PB의 cross-collection auth manageRule와 다르다. 익명 공개 record 경로는 Anonymous principal fallback으로 존재하므로 부재로 판단하지 않았다.

feature: OIDC userInfo 없는 id_token 기반 로그인
pbContract: userinfo URL이 없으면 id_token claims를 사용한다. audience/time 검증과 선택적 issuer allowlist/JWKS 서명 검증을 지원하고 표준 name/username/picture 및 bool-like verified를 추출한다.
pgImplementation: userinfo 미설정 시 mandatory issuer/JWKS, RS256 signature/kid/audience/azp/expiry/nonce를 검사한 뒤 generic claim mapping으로 로그인한다.
gap: 안전한 제한적 fallback은 존재하지만 mandatory JWKS/nonce, RS256-only와 bool-only generic email_verified, 필수 email decode, name/username 미매핑으로 PB의 지원 provider/claim 범위를 전부 표현하지 못한다.

feature: OAuth 신규 가입 createRule·required field 적용
pbContract: OAuth 신규 사용자는 createData/mapped fields로 내부 POST collection records를 수행해 createRule와 동일 field validation을 통과해야 한다.
pgImplementation: 신규 OAuth identity는 registration flags와 email collision을 검사한 뒤 users와 identity를 직접 insert하고 authRule를 검사한다.
gap: 정적 경로상 registrationEnabled=true 및 허용 authRule일 때 createRule=false/required custom field가 OAuth 신규 가입에 적용되지 않는 것으로 보인다. 이 조합을 실행 재현한 결과는 없으며 기존 테스트는 authRule과 realm 격리만 검사한다.

feature: verification token invalidation after an email-only account update
pbContract: PB verification confirmation rejects a token whose email claim no longer matches the record; record saves also rotate tokenKey on email changes, invalidating existing signed record tokens.
pgImplementation: Verification token issuance stores no email payload; confirmation matches active user, purpose, expiry, unused state and a digest of current password hash, then sets verified. Email-only typed auth-record updates delete sessions but the reviewed path does not invalidate pending email-action rows.
gap: Static concern, not an executed reproduction or confirmed vulnerability: after issuing a still-valid verification token, an administrator/authorized manager changes only the email without changing the password; old-token confirmation appears able to verify the new address because no original-email comparison/invalidation is visible in the reviewed path. No regression test for that exact sequence was located. Reproduce under controlled fixtures before treating impact as established.

feature: verification trust-transition cleanup of old password and OAuth links
pbContract: When verification changes an existing record from unverified to verified, PB randomizes the password if password auth is disabled. Its verified-upgrade model hook deletes pre-existing external auth links transactionally and rotates tokenKey when links existed.
pgImplementation: ConfirmVerification updates only verified and updated_at inside email-token consumption. No password randomization, pre-existing OAuth identity cleanup or session revocation is visible in that operation; the existing successful verification test intentionally retains the session.
gap: The reviewed verification transition does not implement PB's password and pre-existing external-auth cleanup. This is a static contract difference; exploitability or resulting account compromise has not been reproduced. PgBase tests cover verified state and single-use token handling, not these cleanup conditions.

pbContract: Global SMTP settings expose enabled, host, port, username/password, TLS, AUTH PLAIN or LOGIN, and optional EHLO/HELO localName; sender display name/address and app metadata are global settings. SMTP-disabled fallback is assessed separately in MAIL-06.
pgImplementation: Process-wide SMTP options and per-auth-collection encrypted SMTP credentials support address/from, username/password, serverName, implicit TLS, timeout and explicitly local insecure development mode. Blank submitted passwords preserve existing stored secrets; API reads redact them.
gap: The transport implements smtp.PlainAuth only and exposes no AUTH LOGIN selector or custom EHLO localName. TLS policy is deliberately stricter off-loopback. Global settings JSON, sender display-name metadata and realm configuration are not interchangeable with PB.

pbContract: Each auth collection stores five configurable HTML email templates: verification, password reset, email change, OTP and auth alert, with subject/body and built-in defaults.
pgImplementation: Per-auth-collection mail templates accept verify/password_reset/email_change/otp/auth_alert, each with subject, required text body and optional HTML body. All five have active service send paths; HTML is wrapped and ordinary attachments can be supplied through hooks.
gap: PB template fields/default HTML/layout are not drop-in compatible with PgBase's purpose identifiers and required text/placeholder validation. No-template actions use simple native text fallbacks; auth alerts require an explicitly stored template. Placeholder capability is separately partial in MAIL-03.

pbContract: PB resolves {APP_NAME}, {APP_URL}, {TOKEN}, {OTP}, {OTP_ID}, {ALERT_INFO} and nonhidden {RECORD:field} values in both subject and HTML body; string record values are escaped. Default action links target /_/#/auth/confirm-*/<token>.
pgImplementation: Templates interpolate native {{action_url}}, {{otp}}, {{otp_id}} or {{alert}} into body/HTML. Generated action links point to /auth/action#action=...&token=...; page clears the fragment and sends confirmation only on explicit submission.
gap: App metadata, arbitrary nonhidden record placeholders, raw token placeholder and all subject substitution are absent from reviewed rendering paths. Native placeholder/action-link/token syntax differs; copying a PB template does not produce an equivalent rendered message.

pbContract: The settings test-email form takes recipient, a selected one of five auth templates, and optional auth collection (default _superusers), builds a synthetic record, and sends the chosen real rendered template through the normal mail lifecycle.
pgImplementation: Separate administrator endpoints preview a submitted native template using a supplied action URL/sample OTP/alert, and send a fixed 'PgBase SMTP test' message through the collection transport.
gap: SMTP test does not accept a template selector or exercise stored auth-template rendering/record placeholders. Preview and transport smoke test therefore do not implement PB's selected-template test-email contract. A preview-specific regression test was not located in the inspected tests.

pbContract: Each of five auth mails raises MailerRecordEvent with App, Record, replaceable Mailer, mutable Message and action metadata (token/newEmail, otpId/password, info); the generic OnMailerSend hook runs inside the selected client's Send call after the purpose event.
pgImplementation: Generic mail.send and purpose-specific hooks can veto or mutate delivery and receive paired outcomes; MailEvent provides Purpose, Message and Meta. OTP and alert services supply metadata, and the decorator wraps both configured SMTP and injected senders.
gap: Purpose events do not expose PB Record or replaceable Mailer/App. Verification/reset/email-change sends do not populate token/newEmail Meta. Generic hook precedes purpose hooks, reversing PB order. These are behavioral hook-contract gaps beyond naming differences.

feature: automatic sendmail fallback when SMTP is disabled
pbContract: App.NewMailClient returns the built-in Sendmail transport when global SMTP.Enabled is false; Sendmail locates and invokes the system sendmail executable.
pgImplementation: Mailer selection uses a per-realm SMTP configuration or an explicitly configured process sender; absence of both returns 'user email actions unavailable'. No built-in sendmail selection/transport was found in internal/mailer, email options or sender setup.
gap: Deployments relying on the host sendmail command require custom sender integration or SMTP configuration. This omitted transport feature cannot be inferred from generic SMTP support.

feature: generic mail envelope, inline attachments and HTML-only messages
pbContract: PB Message supports per-message named From, multiple To/Cc/Bcc, arbitrary headers, regular and inline attachment readers, text and/or HTML; SMTP derives plain text from HTML when Text is empty.
pgImplementation: Native Message and script mail bridge support one recipient, subject, required text, optional HTML and bounded ordinary attachments; sender is transport-owned. SMTP encodes multipart alternative/mixed and limits total attachment bytes to 8 MiB.
gap: No native Cc/Bcc/multiple recipients, per-message From, custom headers or inline attachment fields. HTML-only messages are rejected because Text is mandatory, instead of PB's HTML-to-text fallback. Ordinary attachment tests do not establish these missing envelope capabilities.

pbContract: Collections have independent nullable list/view/create/update/delete rule strings; nonempty rules filter the corresponding operation.
pgImplementation: Five persisted typed AST actions, PocketBase string import/export adapter, transaction-bound row evaluation, and native owner defaults are implemented. Collection admission remains an additional independent opt-in gate.
gap: Different storage and admission model; absence of stored policy means owner-only, while PB collection rules default to locked. This row establishes five-action capability, not syntax or wire equivalence.

pbContract: Rules support field comparisons and request auth fields, including arbitrary literal comparisons against @request.auth.id; record ownership is expressed through fields rather than a built-in ownership side table.
pgImplementation: Native owner/authenticated/all/any/comparison AST and PB field-to-auth-ID comparisons exist. The parser special-cases auth ID empty-string equality into authenticated/unauthenticated predicates.
gap: @request.auth.id = 'nonempty-id' is rejected by accessRuleComparison, despite being valid PB. Native owner is intentionally different from id = @request.auth.id; tests correctly keep them distinct. Existing tests cover empty ID/field references, not arbitrary literal ID equality.

pbContract: PB filter strings support quoted literals, request operands, relation/back-relation/collection references, modifiers, functions, and identifier macros.
pgImplementation: Catalog-aware PB AST/compiler supports many comparisons, relations, JSON paths, any/each semantics, geoDistance, strftime and selected UTC macros. A compatibility rules endpoint parses PB strings.
gap: Not full PB grammar: access-rule parsing calls parseFilterRequest without the double-quote normalization used by the record-query compatibility path, so PB double-quoted rule literals fail. Only selected date macros are supported. More critically, ValidateRules supplies nil request context for list/view/delete, so request-variable rules such as @request.method = 'GET' cannot be saved there; create/update use empty request maps and reject auth literals. The broad conformance test directly inserts policy SQL and therefore does not test this save boundary.

pbContract: A null rule locks the action to superusers, an empty string opens it, and a nonempty expression filters records. Locked state is different from an expression that matches no rows.
pgImplementation: PB rule adapter round-trips null as deny and empty string as allow. Auth collection rule storage separately preserves nullable strings. Native record execution combines these predicates with collection admission.
gap: Base-record null is lowered to the same deny AST used for ordinary filtering, losing the locked-versus-filter distinction at execution. A null-derived list rule produces 200 empty when collection admission is enabled; PB returns 403. Empty allow also does not open PgBase without its independent admission opt-in. Auth null/empty tests only demonstrate auth storage and selected session paths.

pbContract: After credentials succeed and on refresh, AuthRule filters the authenticating record using the original HTTP RequestInfo; @request.auth is the preexisting caller, not automatically the authenticating target. Null locks authentication; empty allows. Refusal is 403.
pgImplementation: Nullable persisted authRule is evaluated before transaction-bound session issuance, OAuth/OTP/MFA credential consumption and refresh. Current custom fields and auth-to-auth relations are supported.
gap: Session evaluation always makes the authenticating target the principal and supplies no original HTTP method/query/header/body/context. Thus rules involving @request.auth or request metadata differ, including @request.auth.id != '' during an unauthenticated password login. PgBase returns invalid_credentials/401 rather than PB 403. The auth resolver loads only auth collections, so @collection/base-record relation reachability is also narrower. Tests verify target-field allow/deny and rollback, not original-caller/request-context parity.

pbContract: An authenticated caller satisfying a nonempty manageRule gains auth-record manager privileges after create/update access passes. Empty/null grants no manager access. Ordinary permitted self password updates can use oldPassword without manage privileges; manager rules may inspect auth from another collection.
pgImplementation: Delegated update evaluates distinct actor and target, requires update rule plus manage rule for email/password/verified/active changes, revokes affected credentials, and uses deleteRule for deletion. Empty manage grants no privileges.
gap: Actor lookup is hard-bound to the target auth collection; tests explicitly assert cross-realm managers are rejected, unlike PB's rule-controlled request auth. Authorized auth-record password updates always require manageRule and do not accept the PB oldPassword alternative through this record mutation path. Separate account password-change APIs are not the same record-update contract.

pbContract: Collection administration stores and validates PB filter strings through collection rule fields; the resolver evaluates those strings with request and catalog context. PB does not define PgBase's dedicated unsaved-row preview endpoint.
pgImplementation: Admin GET/PUT offers native AST and ?compat=pocketbase strings. The preview backend can evaluate an unsaved single rule against up to 50 records, including relations and supplied request context.
gap: Older claim that backend relation/request preview is absent is stale. UI still edits raw AST and supplies no request context editor. Its save adapter sends {rules, revision}, while native PUT strictly decodes a struct with only rules. Preview sends JSON.parse(draft), the full five-action Rules object, as one rule instead of selecting draft[previewAction]. The UI mock tests do not assert these bodies against actual endpoint decoding. PB text editing and usable end-to-end save/preview are not established.

feature: rule denial HTTP status and result contract (omission)
pbContract: Locked action:403; nonmatching list:200 empty; failed create predicate:400; failed view/update/delete predicate:404; failed authRule:403.
pgImplementation: Record predicate failures hide existing rows with 404 and list predicates filter before pagination. Create denial maps to ErrDenied/403. Authentication rule failure maps to invalid_credentials/401.
gap: Create predicate and authRule statuses differ from PB, and null-lock distinction is lost for base-row list/view/update/delete. Existing integration test explicitly expects 403 on create predicate denial, so this is a documented implementation difference, not proof of PB conformance.

feature: actual request environment and auth projection (omission)
pbContract: @request.context is a scalar with default/expand/realtime/protectedFile/batch/oauth2/otp/password values. @request.auth exposes current auth record fields and relations; method/body/query/normalized headers derive from the real request, and absent values resolve NULL.
pgImplementation: Record HTTP creates method/query/normalized-header maps, four auth fields (id/email/verified/created), and a Context object containing requestId. Compiler supports @request.context.<key> and requires explicit auth-map keys.
gap: PB scalar @request.context = 'default' cannot be represented by the PgBase dotted Context map. Custom auth fields/collection identity/relations are absent from real record HTTP auth context; missing auth keys cause compilation errors instead of PB NULL semantics. Conformance tests manually construct a richer RequestContext and do not establish actual HTTP wiring parity.

pbContract: Authenticated superusers bypass collection record rules, including locked null rules.
pgImplementation: Administrator operations bypass row rules. PgBase additionally has scoped service principals: collection/action grants are checked, then service principals bypass user row predicates.
gap: Administrator behavior has a corresponding PB role, but scoped service bypass is a PgBase extension without a PB-equivalent role. The listed integration test uses administrator rule administration; it is not a dedicated bypass conformance test.

feature: hidden fields in stored API rules (omission)
pbContract: Stored API rules can reference hidden fields; allowHiddenFields=true is used during rule compilation, then restricted only for unprivileged client search filters.
pgImplementation: The PB catalog resolver rejects hidden non-relation fields unconditionally. Native typed AST field resolution can still address scalar hidden fields, so the missing portion is PB rule-string/catalog behavior.
gap: A valid PB stored rule such as hidden_status = 'published' cannot be saved/compiled through PgBase's PB rule path. PB explicitly tests a hidden title in a stored listRule; no corresponding PgBase parity assertion was found in inspected tests.

pbContract: @collection.<nameOrId>:<alias>.<field> resolves collection identity separately from a stable join alias. Repeated aliases use the same joined row; distinct aliases permit separate joined rows.
pgImplementation: Unaliased @collection.name.field resolves a catalog name and compiles per-comparison multi-value EXISTS/NOT EXISTS predicates. Forward and reverse relations are supported.
gap: ResolveCollection performs exact name lookup and has no nameOrId/alias handling. Shared-row correlation across multiple @collection comparisons is not proven by existing tests, which use only one such comparison per policy; compiler structure uses separate subqueries. A PB alias rule cannot be imported as-is. Potential cross-row differences require focused executable differential tests before assigning a security impact.

feature: predicate NULL/empty and explicit LIKE wildcard semantics (omission)
pbContract: For ordinary non-JSON operands, PB equality normalizes null and empty string and inequality is NULL-aware; JSON extraction can disable fallback. LIKE wraps unpatterned literal text but preserves explicit unescaped percent wildcard placement.
pgImplementation: PB SQL compiler treats null literals as IS NULL/IS NOT NULL and other comparisons as COALESCE(lhs op rhs,false); contains always emits '%' || rhs || '%'.
gap: Ordinary null/empty equality is not PB-compatible; current PgBase test explicitly keeps title=null distinct from title=''. LIKE 'prefix%' becomes '%prefix%' instead of retaining prefix anchoring. Existing tests cover basic contains/null cases, not PB explicit wildcard and NULL fallback fixtures. These differences can change which records a policy grants.
